provenance: Technique IDs, names, tactics, and parent relationships in this exercise subset were checked against the official MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise STIX release tagged v15.1. Descriptions are concise educational summaries, not a copy of the complete STIX catalogue.

records.name: Phishing
records.description: Adversaries may send phishing messages to gain access to victim systems. A message being received alone does not establish phishing or user interaction.

records.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
records.description: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands, scripts, or binaries.

records.name: PowerShell
records.description: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution. A process observation alone does not establish malicious use.

records.name: Process Discovery
records.description: Adversaries may attempt to get information about running processes on a system.

records.name: Security Software Discovery
records.description: Adversaries may attempt to list security software, configurations, defensive tools, and sensors installed on a system or cloud environment.

records.name: Software Discovery
records.description: Adversaries may attempt to list software and software versions installed on a system or in a cloud environment.

records.name: System Information Discovery
records.description: An adversary may attempt to collect detailed information about the operating system and hardware.

records.name: Valid Accounts
records.description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials for existing accounts. An unfamiliar successful sign-in alone is insufficient to establish credential abuse.

records.name: Cloud Accounts
records.description: Valid accounts in cloud environments may be used to achieve initial access, persistence, privilege escalation, or defense evasion.
